statement: Two straight lines intersect, forming four angles. One of the angles measures $(3x + 20)^\circ$, and the angle vertical to it measures $(5x - 16)^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of an angle adjacent to the $(3x + 20)^\circ$ angle?

choices.misconception: I solved $3x + 20 = 5x - 16$ correctly but reported $x$ instead of an angle measure.
I found the measure of the $(3x + 20)^\circ$ angle itself, 74, instead of the angle next to it.
I treated the vertical angles as supplementary, so $8x + 4 = 180$ gave $x = 22$, an angle of 86 and a neighbor of 94.

hints: Set the two expressions equal to find $x$. An adjacent angle forms a straight line with the first angle.
From $3x + 20 = 5x - 16$, $x = 18$, so the angle is $74^\circ$. The adjacent angle is $180 - 74$.

solutions.reliable: Vertical angles are congruent, so $3x + 20 = 5x - 16$, which gives $2x = 36$ and $x = 18$. The angle measures $3(18) + 20 = 74$ degrees. An adjacent angle forms a linear pair with it, so it measures $180 - 74 = 106$ degrees.
